1.explanation:
1. We use ESLint’s programmatic API (CLIEngine) so that you can reproduce exactly the same rule configuration as your CLI invocation.  
2. We set useEslintrc: false and supply a baseConfig with only the no-constant-condition rule set to “error”.  
3. We pass in the two code snippets (an if-statement with a literal and a function call with a ternary literal) exactly as in the bug report.  
4. When you run node reproduce.js, you will get a JSON report that shows the ruleId “no-constant-condition” fires twice, and you will see that the reported location (start/end lines and columns) covers the entire statement/expression rather than just the constant portion.  

This minimal script isolates the bug in ESLint 4.8.0 and lets you inspect the ranges programmatically.
1.bug_scenario:
In both cases shown in the screenshot ESLint’s “no-constant-condition” rule underlines the entire statement or expression, not just the literal constant (“true” or the ternary expression).  
– In the first example the red underline spans from the “if” through the closing “}” instead of highlighting only the word “true”.  
– In the second example the underline spans the entire call “something(true ? 1 : 0);” instead of just the ternary sub-expression “true ? 1 : 0”.
